newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Doughty Hanson plans sale of TAG Heuer shares.
newsitem.headline: Doughty Hanson plans sale of TAG Heuer shares.

text.p: Doughty Hanson & Co said in a statement that funds it manages planned to sell approximately 690,000 shares of TAG Heuer International S.A. representing 12.8 percent of the company's outstanding shares.
"The sale will be by the way of a marketed offering due to be completed in the week of August 25," it said.
Doughty Hanson said that the offering would coincide with a roadshow for institutional investors which is being organised by TAG Heuer following release of its first half results.
Doughty Hanson was involved in the recapitalisation of TAG Heuer in December 1995. This was followed by TAG Heuer's initial public offering (IPO) last year.
"Funds managed by Doughty Hanson & Co Ltd sold a portion of their holdings in TAG Heuer International SA in conjunction with the IPO," Doughty Hanson said.
"This (latest) offering represents the sale of substantially all of the remainder of those holdings," Doughty Hanson said.
TAG Heuer's shares were listed on the Swiss Stock Exchange last September and its American Depository Shares (ADS) on the New York Stock Exchange.
TAG Heuer reported on Friday that its net income rose 60.4 percent in the first half of 1997 to 25.5 million Swiss francs, from 15.9 million in the first half of 1996.
It said net sales in the first half rose 6.6 percent to 226.2 million francs from 212.2 million in the first half of 1996.
Its shares closed on the Swiss Stock Exchange on Thursday at 229.00 Swiss francs.
